criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: The taxonomy contains the major decision points implied by the use case, each with its main candidate decisions.
criteria.reason: The taxonomy covers the main decision areas implied by the use case with multiple candidates: server redundancy and failure tolerance in 21 Replica Topology, replication mechanisms in 22 Replica Synchronization Mechanism, write coordination in 30 Replica Write Coordination, placement and read scaling in 13 Repository Placement and Read Routing, storage maintenance in 12 Compaction Maintenance Technique, large-repository transfer in 6 Large-Repository Object Acquisition, and client scalability in 9 Client Repository Performance Strategy. Verification choices are also represented in 27 Replica State Comparison. No major use-case area lacks a decision point with several candidate decisions; the main revision opportunity is only to reorganize the crowded alternatives in 30, not to add coverage.

criteria.name: Use case alignment
criteria.description: Every dimension serves the stated use case; none is out of its scope.
criteria.reason: All eight dimensions are within the use case's scope: replica topology, synchronization, write coordination, placement and read routing address hosting-server scalability for many repositories and users; compaction and replica-state comparison address large-scale repository storage and reliability; large-repository object acquisition and client repository performance address client-side scalability. No dimension is unrelated to Git architecture, the stated lifecycle, or the server/client focus.

criteria.name: No catch-alls
criteria.description: No dimension or value is a vague catch-all ('Other', 'Miscellaneous', 'General', 'Other approaches').
criteria.reason: No catch-all dimensions or values were found. The taxonomy uses specific decision points such as Replica Topology, Compaction Maintenance Technique, Large-Repository Object Acquisition, and Replica State Comparison, with concrete alternatives and outcomes rather than labels like “Other,” “Miscellaneous,” or “General considerations.” No reorganization is needed for this criterion.

criteria.name: Axis vs. value
criteria.description: Each dimension is a decision point with alternatives, not a single option presented as a dimension; each value is an option, not a sub-topic.
criteria.reason: Several dimensions are genuine decision points, such as 21 Replica Topology and 22 Replica Synchronization Mechanism, but major dimensions bundle multiple decisions. Split 30 Replica Write Coordination into separate dimensions for write-acceptance/ordering, commit and transaction protocol, replication fan-out, and coordination optimizations, moving values such as 30.2, 30.3, 30.8, and 30.11 accordingly. Split 9 Client Repository Performance Strategy into client architecture, maintenance scheduling, filesystem/index handling, and background fetch/commit-graph decisions; its values 9.6, 9.15, 9.18, and 9.23 are sub-decisions rather than alternatives to one strategy question. Split 13 Repository Placement and Read Routing into placement and read-routing dimensions. Also separate 6 Large-Repository Object Acquisition's transfer method from cache-server topology and deployment conditions, and refine 27 Replica State Comparison so checksum choice is distinct from incremental-versus-full checksum maintenance.

criteria.name: One decision point
criteria.description: Each dimension is a single decision point: all its candidate decisions are alternative answers to one question, rather than a broad topic bundling several questions. Where the use case names quality attributes or forces, dimensions whose choice is driven by recognizable quality attributes or trade-offs are preferred (quality-attribute grounding).
criteria.reason: Several dimensions are valid decision points, such as 21 Replica Topology, 12 Compaction Maintenance Technique, 22 Replica Synchronization Mechanism, and 27 Replica State Comparison, each with at least two candidate decisions. However, major dimensions mix different questions. Split 30 Replica Write Coordination into separate coordination protocol, reference-update atomicity, push fan-out, and locking decisions, moving existing values so each resulting dimension retains at least two candidates. Split 9 Client Repository Performance Strategy into client delivery approach, working-tree/index mechanisms, and maintenance scheduling; its values currently mix architecture choices, individual features, implementation techniques, and outcomes. Split 6 Large-Repository Object Acquisition into object-transfer strategy/protocol and cache-server deployment, moving 6.5 and 6.9 to the latter. Split 13 Repository Placement and Read Routing into placement/state-location decisions and read-routing decisions. These broad mixed-question dimensions substantially violate the requirement that every dimension's candidates answer one question.

criteria.name: Rejected-alternative handling
criteria.description: For each candidate decision, the taxonomy makes clear whether sources adopted it, rejected it, or disagree (status 'accepted', 'rejected' or 'mixed'); a rejected alternative is never presented as adopted; each candidate decision appears once with its stance; outcomes (status 'outcome') are kept apart from candidate decisions.
criteria.reason: All values use valid statuses, and most rejected, accepted, and outcome descriptions are consistent. However, several mixed candidates are stated as adopted: 22.1 'Spokes repository replication', 6.6 'Packfile-based Git networking', and 9.12 'Persistent Scalar dependency' should explicitly reflect source disagreement or be given a stance consistent with their descriptions. Value 6.1 'Complete object transfer' is phrased as an alternative acquisition strategy but marked as an outcome; reclassify it as a candidate decision. Value 6.3 'Repository-size threshold for GVFS deployment' describes a deployment decision or criterion rather than an effect, so reclassify it as a candidate decision or move it under an existing decision where it is an outcome.

criteria.name: Dimensional coverage
criteria.description: Every sampled passage that discusses a design decision can be placed under at least one decision point (dimension) of the taxonomy.
criteria.reason: Most decision-bearing passages map to the taxonomy, including client optimization in dimension 9, replication mechanisms in dimension 22, placement and routing in dimension 13, and write coordination in dimension 30. The main gaps are s03_p07 and s03_p08, which decide to quiesce servers, preserve long-running reads, and use controlled rolling reboots or retirement instead of abrupt shutdowns; add a dimension such as “Planned Server Maintenance Strategy” with values for quiescing and rolling retirement. s01_p04 discusses rejecting distributed filesystems such as NFS because of filesystem-semantic and performance problems, which is not represented by 22.2 “DRBD block-level replication”; add a rejected “Distributed filesystem replication” value to dimension 22, supported by s01_p03 and s01_p04.

criteria.name: Candidate-decision coverage
criteria.description: The options that the sampled passages adopt or reject are named as values (candidate decisions) of the right dimension.
criteria.reason: The taxonomy covers many adopted or rejected options, including DRBD rejection and Git-and-rsync replication (22.2, 22.3), three replicas and majority coordination (21.2, 30.1), background maintenance and fetches (9.5, 9.18), partial clone (6.7), and rendezvous-hashed placement (13.4). Important specific options are missing: add a sparse-checkout/cone-mode value and the /src working-directory layout to dimension 9, supported by s04_p02 and s05_p04; add a multi-pack-index maintenance value to dimension 12, supported by s04_p02 and s05_p12; add a WAL-in-S3 source-of-truth/CAS replication value to dimension 22, supported by s01_p11; add bookkeeping-update coalescing and user-update prioritization to dimension 30, supported by s02_p06; and add a planned-maintenance dimension covering quiescing, rolling rack reboots, and graceful retirement/repair, supported by s03_p07, s03_p08, and s03_p09.

criteria.name: Value exclusivity
criteria.description: Each system (source) adopts one value per dimension: the values of a dimension are alternatives, not features used together. Deterministic: computed from the evidence, without a judge.
criteria.reason:
- Dimension 9 'Client Repository Performance Strategy': 3 of 3 sources adopt several of its values. Values 9.2 'Native Git scalability improvements' and 9.8 'Core Git capability consolidation' are adopted together by s01, s04, s05 (passages s01_p10, s01_p16, s04_p01).
- Dimension 13 'Repository Placement and Read Routing': 3 of 3 sources adopt several of its values. Values 13.4 'Rendezvous-hashed repository routing' and 13.5 'Stale-routing recovery' are adopted together by s01, s03 (passages s01_p11, s03_p04).
- Dimension 30 'Replica Write Coordination': 3 of 3 sources adopt several of its values. Values 30.1 'Strict-majority coordinated writes' and 30.2 'Three-phase commit coordination' are adopted together by s01, s02 (passages s01_p07, s01_p08, s01_p09).
- Dimension 6 'Large-Repository Object Acquisition': 2 of 3 sources adopt several of its values. Values 6.4 'GVFS demand-driven transfer' and 6.7 'Partial clone transfer' are adopted together by s04, s05 (passages s04_p01, s04_p02, s05_p01).
Values one source uses together are not alternatives. Split such a dimension into the questions its values answer (every part keeps at least two candidate decisions), move a value to the existing dimension whose question it answers, or merge two values that are the same option.
